correctness.rationale: For the stated identical Beverton–Holt map write h(z)=Tz/(1+z), H(z)=h(z)tanh(k(z-u)), u=T-1. The sum equation at any asymmetric positive fixed point forces x>u>y after swapping; strict Jensen gives m=(x+y)/2<u. Then t=u-y>s=x-u>0, so h(x)s+h(y)t=u(s+t)+s²/(T+s)-t²/(T-t)<u(s+t). Using tanh(v)<v rules out the stationary difference when ku≤1, including equality. For every ku>1 solve the sum equation for x(y)>u on 0<y<u; the difference quotient tends to 0 and ku at the endpoints, so crosses 1. The analytic mean equation gives m=u-d²/(uT)+O(d⁴) and the odd difference equation has a positive cubic saturation beta=(1/3+(u+2)/T²)/u². On the emerging pair the critical eigenvalue is ku-3 beta d²+O(d⁴)=1-2(ku-1)+O((ku-1)²): the off-diagonal coupling contributes h''(u)H''(u)/(1-1/T) to the d² coefficient, equal to -2H''(u)/(uT), in addition to the diagonal term. The other eigenvalue stays near 1/T. The symmetric multipliers are 1/T and ku; at extinction constant column sums and positivity give spectral radius T. No nonlinear stability at equality, uniqueness of a remote pair, or stability for every ku>1 is inferred. RESULT.md §§1–6 checked; verify.py and VERIFICATION.md inspected, not executed. Their finite parameter checks are not used to prove the threshold.

value.rationale: The sharp all-parameter equilibrium boundary (including the neutral endpoint), stable nearby nonuniform states, and strict biomass loss together distinguish mechanisms that an extinction-based persistence criterion cannot see. In particular, below-threshold global exclusion and above-threshold existence at arbitrarily large k are not a routine local pitchfork calculation. This is a useful exact benchmark for discrete density-dependent dispersal, not a generic claim about ecosystems.
